newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Two badly hurt in explosions in Goma.
newsitem.headline: Two badly hurt in explosions in Goma.

text.p: Two explosions rocked a suburb of rebel-held Goma in eastern Zaire on Saturday, badly wounding two people, witnesses said.
The second explosion was probably caused by an incoming mortar round from the direction of Mugunga camp where Rwandan Hutu refugees are massed, Reuters correspondent Christian Jennings said.
Rwanda's state radio said earlier on Saturday that fighting was taking place around Mugunga as Hutu fighters tried to resist advancing rebels.

Jennings said two Zairean civilians, a woman and a man, were badly wounded when their house in the western suburbs was damaged by one of the explosions. Foreign journalists took the couple to hospital.
Goma was quiet before the evening explosions.

Mugunga camp to the west of Goma is out of reach of journalists and beyond rebel lines. Thousands of ex-Rwandan soldiers and Interahamwe militiamen, all Hutus who helped commit the genocide in Rwanda in 1994, are believed to be inside the camp.

The well-armed fighters fought alongside Zaire's ramshackle army in a vain attempt to retain control of Goma last week. About 500 people died in the battle won by the rebels and troops from the present, Tutsi-dominated Rwandan government army.

About one million Rwandan Hutu refugees are in eastern Zaire where they fled after the genocide of up to one million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus. For the past two years the huge majority have refused to go home, fearing reprisals.
But about 120 of the refugees arrived in Goma on Saturday after walking for more than a week with no food or water except what they could scavenge by the roadside.
The refugees, the first significant group to arrive in Goma since it fell to the rebels, said some of their number had died along the way.
They said they had fled from the two camps of Katale and Kahindo attacked by rebels a week and a half ago and were not prevented by the Interahamwe militiamen from making for Rwanda.
"There were people who died of thirst and exhaustion on the way, but we did not see anybody with any traces of cholera yet," said Charles Kairwa, 32.
"I left Katale the Thursday before last with 22 people in my family group. Only 12 made it, the rest are somewhere back at the side of the road.
"We saw the Interahamwe militias but they let us pass. Most of the Interahamwe from Katale and Kahindo have moved to Mugunga, which they say they will defend."
All 120 refugees, who were given biscuits by aid workers on arrival, moved from the centre of Goma to the border with Gisenyi where they were attempting to cross to Rwanda.
